midterms.context: Iraq War dominated the election. Mark Foley congressional page scandal broke weeks before Election Day. Nancy Pelosi became the first female Speaker. Democrats flipped both chambers simultaneously for the first time since 1986.

Largest House swing since 1938 and the biggest midterm loss since Truman in 1946. 9.8% unemployment and ACA backlash fuelled the Tea Party movement. Census-year election gave Republicans sweeping redistricting power for a decade.

Second-term Obama drag. Oct 2013 government shutdown initially hurt Republicans but Democrats couldn't capitalise. Record-low turnout of 36.4%. Republicans flipped the Senate for the first time since 2006. Ebola fears and ISIS dominated the final weeks.

Democrats flipped 41 House seats driven by suburban college-educated women voters. The economy was strong but anti-Trump sentiment dominated. Republicans held and expanded Senate majority in a very favourable map — only 9 R seats vs 26 D seats up for election.

Expected red wave failed to materialise. Dobbs decision overturning Roe v. Wade energised Democratic turnout especially among women and young voters. Republicans eked out a 9-seat House majority but significantly underperformed polling. Democrats gained a Senate seat in Pennsylvania.
